ut_el_diablo_wall.blurb: El Diablo Wall is the lower of the steep limestone walls in the Hell Area of American Fork Canyon, just beneath Hell Cave. It is a short, powerful face where the climbing is almost entirely bolted sport, bouldery and demanding on the fingers. Nearly everything here is 5.12 or harder, with the bulk of the climbs in the 5.13 and 5.14 range and only a couple of easier lines to warm up on. The area has a long reputation as a local training ground for strong sport climbers along the Wasatch Front, and it is also remembered as an early home of limestone sport climbing in the United States. Expect to share the wall on good days.

ut_early_bird_crag_the.blurb: The Early Bird Crag is a sport-climbing wall of cobbled conglomerate along the main road through Maple Canyon. It faces east, so it catches the sun from the first light of morning and tends to feel hot, which keeps traffic low compared with the shadier walls nearby. The routes are almost all single-pitch bolted lines, running from very easy up through 5.11, with a good handful of 5.8 to 5.11 climbs in between, so it works for mixed groups. A few longer multi-pitch lines also start here. Come early in warm weather, and pick another wall when the afternoon heat sets in.
ut_early_bird_crag_the.parking_note: Leave the car by the bridge on the canyon road, then step over the creek on the north side and head for the base of the wall.
ut_early_bird_crag_the.approach: Walk east along the foot of the cliff until you reach the sunny east-facing section. The first routes you pass are the multi-pitch lines.

ut_diamond_the_2.blurb: The Diamond is a large limestone shield in the Utah Hills, west of St. George, at roughly 6,000 feet. It faces northwest, so the wall stays in shade through the morning and picks up sun in the afternoon, which makes it a comfortable choice in the warmer parts of the year. Every route here is bolted sport climbing, and the grades cluster in the 5.10 to 5.12 range with a couple of 5.13s on top. The wall feels secluded and steep, the ledge at the base is small and tight against the rock, and the walk up is on a steep old road. It is better suited to adults than to young children.
ut_diamond_the_2.approach: From where you leave the vehicle, hike the steep old road uphill. A cairned climbing trail peels off to the left toward the wall.

ut_coal_pit_buttress.blurb: Coalpit Buttress sits on the south side of Little Cottonwood Canyon, between the Triangle Wall and the Pentapitch area, in the canyon's quartz monzonite, a rock much like white granite. It is mostly a trad crag, known for multi-pitch routes that follow cracks, friction slabs and black roofs, with a few steep sport pitches mixed in and some aid. Most of the free climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. It is a good place to hunt for shade on a hot summer day, though the sun does reach parts of it at some hours. Plan on a real approach over talus.

ut_compound_the.blurb: The Compound is the hard-sport crag of Maple Canyon, a steep, north-facing cave and wall of cobbled conglomerate that sits high above the trees. The routes are fairly short, topping out around 60 feet below a big shelf, and the climbing is powerful, sitting between the bouldery style of Box Canyon and the long endurance pitches elsewhere in the canyon. Almost everything is bolted, and the grades are concentrated in the 5.13s, with a number of 5.12s and 5.14s alongside and very little below 5.11. The road in has almost no shade, so a summer visit means walking in the sun. Cleaning is ongoing, so avoid standing under other climbers.
ut_compound_the.parking_note: Without four-wheel drive, stop at the upper end of the smooth part of the canyon road near the Right Fork trailhead. High-clearance vehicles can sometimes go farther up the rough road.

ut_habitado.blurb: Habitado is a quieter sandstone crag in Indian Creek, a short walk from the busy Supercrack parking area but out of the main flow of traffic. The climbs here are shorter and less traveled than on the famous walls nearby, and almost all of them are trad crack climbs. The grades are weighted toward 5.10, with a fair number of 5.11s and a few easier and harder options on either side. It is a handy place to escape the crowds or to settle in on the Creek's style of crack climbing without waiting in line. Bring a plan for human waste, as facilities are limited, and stay off the rock when it is wet.
ut_habitado.parking_note: Use the Supercrack parking area as your starting point.
ut_habitado.approach: Head east through the wash on the trail from the Supercrack lot. A very short talus scramble gets you up to the base of the crag.

ut_dry_fork_canyon.blurb: Dry Fork Canyon, north of Vernal, is a secluded sandstone venue at about 7,100 feet with a mix of crack climbing, sport routes and bouldering. Trad and bouldering are about equally represented, with a smaller set of bolted lines. Boulder problems run from the easiest grades up to V5, with one much harder outlier, and the roped routes mostly sit between 5.8 and 5.11. Much of the canyon's rock is still undeveloped, and the quality around Vernal is mixed, so expect an adventurous, low-traffic day with some loose rock and old anchors rather than a polished crag.
ut_dry_fork_canyon.parking_note: Drive north on 3500 West, which turns into the Dry Fork Settlement Road, and continue up into the canyon to the pull-off for the Flume trail. Room there is limited.

vt_lower_west_bolton.blurb: Lower West is one of the most popular and easily reached cliffs in Bolton, a short walk up Notch Road in northern Vermont. The rock is schist, and the routes are short, roughly 30 to 40 feet, with sturdy anchors on top and a path to them, which makes it the go-to place to set up top ropes and teach beginners. Moderates up to 5.10 dominate, most of them trad, and a few of the harder leads feel a bit run-out. A handful of sport lines and boulder problems round it out. Summer and fall weekends and after-work hours get crowded, so watch for people setting up above you.
vt_lower_west_bolton.parking_note: From Route 2 in Bolton, turn onto Notch Road. A small lot a short way up fits about three cars, with a few more spaces along the road beside it.
